newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU takes legal action over British VAT on art.
newsitem.headline: EU takes legal action over British VAT on art.

text.p: The European Commission, acting on complaints from art dealers in other European Union countries, threatened on Thursday to take Britain to court for distorting competition in the art and antiques markets.
The EU executive decided to send a so-called reasoned opinion to London, the second step in its infringement procedure before referring the case to the Luxembourg Court of Justice.

It accused London of failing to comply with EU legislation on value added tax BY applying a rate of 2.5 percent to both the value of imported works of art and the services of auctioneers acting on its territory.

While EU rules allowed the country to apply such a low rate to imports of works of art, collectors' items or antiques until June 30 1999, "the supply of auctioneers' services is a taxable transaction which takes place within the European Union, and as such must be taxed in the United Kingdom at the standard rate of 17.5 percent," the Commission said in a statement.

"The consequences of this unauthorised advantage enjoyed by United Kingdom auctioneers is a severe distortion of competition in relation to other European traders and several complaints have been made to the Commission," it said.
"If there is no change to United Kingdom law within the two months following receipt of the reasoned opinion, the Commission could refer the matter to the Court of Justice."
